chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For Paradise there is a gate called the Gate of the Mujahideen. They proceed towards it, and when they arrive, it is open while they are wearing their swords, the congregation is in the standing position, and the angels are driving them forward. So whoever leaves Jihad, God will clothe him with humiliation and poverty in his livelihood, and destruction in his religion. Indeed, God honored my Ummah with the forelocks of their horses and the thrusts of their spears.'

key_terms.الْمُجَاهِدِينَ: Those who strive in the path of God

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of leaving Jihad according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith underscores the ontological link between martial struggle and spiritual elevation, portraying the gate of 'Al-Mujahideen' as a distinct honor for those who bear arms for God. It connects physical readiness—symbolized by cavalry and spears—to divine honor, while warning that neglecting this duty leads to a triad of losses: humiliation, material poverty, and the erosion of faith. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of Jihad as both a communal obligation and a means of preserving religious integrity.
